name.text: Permutations and Combinations 7 - Does order matter? (drag and drop)

questiontext.text:
For each situation below, decide whether order matters (a permutation) or order does not matter (a combination). Drag the correct label into each box.

  1. A school elects a Prefect and an Assistant Prefect from 10 candidates. [[1]]
  2. A farmer chooses 3 goats out of 8 to take to the market. [[2]]
  3. A 4-digit M-Pesa PIN is made from different digits. [[1]]
  4. A committee of 5 students is chosen from a class of 30. [[2]]
  5. The Gold, Silver and Bronze medals are awarded to 3 of 12 runners. [[1]]
  6. 12 people at a meeting shake hands once with everyone else. [[2]]
  7. 6 different novels are arranged on a library shelf. [[1]]
  8. Two players are picked to carry the ball bag. [[2]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

Ask yourself: if I swap two of the chosen items, do I get a different outcome?

Order matters (permutation): the Prefect and Assistant Prefect roles, the PIN digits, the medal positions and the books on a shelf. Swapping two items gives a different result.

Order does not matter (combination): choosing goats, committee members, handshakes and the two ball-bag carriers. Swapping two items gives the same group.
